title: Fleet entry priming and cache anticipator
creator: Mei Chen
description: Purpose: reduce cold-start latency and meet per-tenant throughput SLOs for Dedicated fleets by introducing a coordinated "anticipator" that stages model parameters and warms KV shards before traffic lands. Background: Dedicated customers require predictable request-per-second and tail-latency guarantees. Current reactive weight pulling and opportunistic KV population cause variable onboarding latency during scale-ups and tenant attach events. Scope: build a Fleet Entry Priming controller that (1) listens to scheduled/expected tenant onramps and autoscaler signals, (2) orchestrates a staged weight load (partial, prioritized layers) onto target nodes, (3) issues KV shard seeding operations using a workload-aware fingerprinting cache strategy, and (4) integrates with admission control to avoid capacity contention with serving traffic. Design constraints: keep memory overhead bounded per-node, avoid duplicated heavyweight weight pulls across replicas, and maintain safety for multi-tenant isolation. Success metrics: reduce median cold-start latency by >=60% for first request after attach, reduce 95th percentile latency by >=40% across scale-up windows, and decrease token-cost overhead of prewarming to <8% of baseline monthly spend. Acceptance criteria: (a) automated controller deployed behind feature flag, (b) demoed for a dedicated fleet with synthetic onboarding pattern, (c) telemetry shows targeted latency improvements and no increase in load-induced OOMs, (d) rollback path and SLA-preserving admission control verified. Implementation notes: use lightweight fingerprint probes to detect cache miss hotsets, stream prioritized parameter slices (embeddings, attention blocks) in order that enables partial inference, and introduce a small, cost-accounted prewarm budget per tenant. Controller will expose metrics for staged residency, probe hit-rate, and prewarm budget consumption. Rollout plan: start with internal canary fleets, validate against SLO dashboards, then open to controlled customer pilots. Post-launch: iterate on heuristics for sequencing and eviction-awareness based on live telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrated median cold-start latency reduction >= 60% on internal fleet
95th percentile cold-start latency reduction >= 40% during scale-ups
Prewarm token-cost <= 8% of baseline monthly spend
No memory safety regressions or increased OOM events
updates: 2026-03-05: Kickoff meeting with serving-runtime, autoscale, and telemetry teams. Agreed success metrics and initial API sketch.
2026-03-07: Prototype for fingerprint probe implemented; microbench shows probe overhead <1% of CPU on warm nodes.
2026-03-09: Benchmarked streaming parameter slices in local cluster; partial inference with first two layers returns coherent tokens at 45% of full-model latency.
2026-03-11: Integration spike with autoscaler signals completed. Added backpressure path so prewarm will back off when replica addition is in progress.
2026-03-13: Internal canary scheduled. Metrics dashboard draft available at provided dashboard link. Next: safety review and adding tests for eviction scenarios.
notes: Coordination required with PM for customer pilot invitations. Plan to include a limited lease-based prewarm budget on tenant billing so customers understand cost tradeoffs.
